evidence.detail: grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(11rem, 1fr)) — auto-fit determines column count dynamically, producing partial final rows when archetype count isn't divisible by that count
Issue author suggests 'disallow 5 and 7 tile wide in css somehow' — CSS media queries with specific column counts (e.g. 2, 3, 4, 6) would prevent non-factor-of-24 widths

triage.fix_sketch: In shared_web/static/css/pd.css, replace the single auto-fit rule (pd.css:2855) with a series of @media breakpoints that set explicit grid-template-columns values — e.g. repeat(2, 1fr) below ~500px, repeat(3, 1fr) below ~700px, repeat(4, 1fr) below ~1000px, repeat(6, 1fr) otherwise — choosing counts that are factors of 24. This removes the ragged-end risk at the cost of tiles growing slightly wider than 11rem at some viewport widths.
triage.notes: The exact breakpoints need visual tuning. The fix is CSS-only and self-contained. Confidence is medium rather than high because the ideal column widths depend on visual inspection at each viewport width.
